payload.task_text:
You are an accreditation coordinator preparing a comprehensive curriculum review for an upcoming university accreditation visit. Your job is to audit the institution's courses against accreditation requirements, find supporting scholarly literature, and document everything in a structured compliance matrix and an accreditation report.

Start by fetching the accreditation requirements from the accreditation portal at http://localhost:30238/api/accreditation_requirements.json. This document specifies minimum thresholds for course counts, faculty ratios, assessment types, and scholarly integration that the institution must meet.

Next, connect to the learning management system and retrieve a list of all courses offered by the institution. For each course, gather the course name, the number of enrolled students, the number of assignments, the number of quizzes the course has (use 0 if it has none), and the number of discussion topics. Also determine how many faculty members (teachers and teaching assistants combined) are associated with each course. Use the course's enrollment count (total students) directly for the number of enrolled students, and derive the faculty count from each course's enrollment records, where faculty are enrollments of type TeacherEnrollment or TaEnrollment.

Using this data, evaluate each course against the accreditation requirements. A course is considered compliant if the student to faculty ratio does not exceed the maximum specified in the requirements and the course has at least one form of assessment (quiz or assignment). Note which courses are compliant and which are not.

Then search the scholarly literature for research supporting the pedagogical approaches used in the curriculum. Search for papers on the following topics: active learning in higher education, assessment best practices in education, online learning effectiveness, curriculum design frameworks, and student engagement strategies. For each topic, find at least one relevant paper and note its title, authors, and relevance to the curriculum.

Create an Excel file called Curriculum_Review.xlsx in your workspace with three sheets. The first sheet should be called "Course Compliance" with columns for Course_Name, Assignment_Count, Quiz_Count, Discussion_Count, Student_Count, Faculty_Count, Student_Faculty_Ratio, and Compliant (Yes or No based on whether the course meets the accreditation criteria). Include all courses.

The second sheet should be called "Literature Support" with columns for Search_Topic, Paper_Title, Authors, and Relevance_Note. Include at least five rows covering the five pedagogical topics listed above.

The third sheet should be called "Summary" with columns for Metric and Value. Include rows for total courses, compliant courses, non-compliant courses, compliance rate (as a percentage), total faculty across all courses, average student to faculty ratio, and the number of supporting papers found.

Finally, create a page in the team's knowledge base (Notion) titled "Accreditation Review Report" (the page title must contain this exact phrase) that summarizes the curriculum audit findings. The page should mention the overall compliance rate, highlight any courses that fail to meet requirements, reference the scholarly literature that supports the institution's pedagogical approach, and note any recommendations for improvement before the accreditation visit.

When you have completed all tasks, call claim_done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one parallel source wave and one parallel writer wave. Canvas and scholarly search are read-only. The main agent fetches the accreditation JSON and freezes the course manifest; writers consume only the merged canonical packet.

Before Wave 1, the main agent fetches http://localhost:30238/api/accreditation_requirements.json once and freezes the literal student-faculty-ratio maximum and assessment-presence rule. It then calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once, validates unique IDs/codes/full names, and freezes the complete 22-course manifest. Partition that manifest into two disjoint shards covering every course_id exactly once: shard A = course_id 1-11 (AAA-2013J through DDD-2013B) and shard B = course_id 12-22 (DDD-2014B through GGG-2014B). Pass each owner its literal ID list, codes, and full names.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Course-metrics owner for shard A (course_id 1-11). For each assigned course, collect the exact full name, enrolled-student count from the course enrollment total, assignment count, quiz count (0 if none), discussion-topic count, and faculty count (TeacherEnrollment plus TaEnrollment only), then mark it compliant when the student-faculty ratio stays within the frozen accreditation maximum and the course has at least one quiz or assignment. Faculty counts must come from actual enrollment records, never inferred from grade rows or current-user metadata; a course lacking source-visible student plus TeacherEnrollment/TaEnrollment coverage gets CONTRACT_BLOCKER_MISSING_ROLE_COMPLETE_ENROLLMENTS and no Faculty_Count, Student_Faculty_Ratio, or Compliant value. Return assigned versus observed course IDs plus the compact per-course rows. Make no writes.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Course-metrics owner for shard B (course_id 12-22) — same literal recipe, only that shard's course identities substituted.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Literature owner for the five fixed pedagogy topics: active learning in higher education; assessment best practices in education; online learning effectiveness; curriculum design frameworks; and student engagement strategies. Find one genuinely relevant paper per topic and return title, authors, and a curriculum-relevance note for each. Read-only; do not write the workbook or Notion page.

After Wave 1, the main agent requires both shards together to cover every frozen course_id exactly once, rejects duplicate/missing IDs, and freezes one canonical packet: all 22 Course Compliance rows, at least five Literature Support rows, and the Summary metrics (total courses, compliant courses, non-compliant courses, compliance rate as a percentage, total faculty across all courses, average student-faculty ratio, supporting-paper count).

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming the canonical packet with no recomputation from Canvas or scholarly search:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Curriculum_Review.xlsx. Create exactly Course Compliance, Literature Support, and Summary with the task's exact headers, all 22 course rows, at least five literature rows, and the frozen summary metrics as literal values. Read every populated range back.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole Notion owner of a page whose title contains the exact phrase Accreditation Review Report. Search exact title first, create at most once on zero matches, block on duplicates, and write a summary of the overall compliance rate, non-compliant courses, scholarly literature supporting the pedagogical approach, and recommendations before the visit. Read the retained page and its child-block text back.

After Wave 2, the main agent reconciles workbook ranges and the Notion read-back against the same packet, then calls claim_done. Do not dispatch an aggregation or verification agent.

You are gathering accreditation audit data from a Canvas LMS. Your assignment: collect exact counts for these courses (given as course_id — known course name): course_id=1 'Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013)', course_id=2 'Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014)', course_id=3 'Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)', course_id=4 'Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014)'

For EACH course in your list, collect:
1. assignment_count: total number of assignments. Use canvas_list_assignments(course_id) and count the entries. If the call errors or returns empty, record 0 and note it.
2. quiz_count: total number of quizzes. Use canvas_list_quizzes(course_id) and count entries. Use 0 if the course has none or the call errors.
3. discussion_count: total number of discussion topics. Use canvas_list_discussion_topics(course_id) and count entries. Use 0 if none.
4. faculty_count: number of faculty associated with the course = enrollments of type TeacherEnrollment or TaEnrollment, derived from the course's enrollment records. Preferred method: canvas_get_course_grades(course_id, type=["TeacherEnrollment","TaEnrollment"], per_page=100, page=1) and keep paging until pagination.has_more is false; count distinct user_ids among returned staff enrollments. If that endpoint returns no staff rows, fall back to canvas_list_course_users(course_id) and count distinct users whose enrollments show role/type TeacherEnrollment or TaEnrollment (state active preferred; if no active staff are returned at all, count inactive ones too and note it).
5. student_count: use the course's total_students field directly (canvas_get_course(course_id) should include it). If the field is missing, count active StudentEnrollment records via canvas_get_course_grades with paging (may be large — page with per_page=100 until pagination.has_more is false).

IMPORTANT: These are large Open University-style courses (up to ~2500 students). Do NOT page through all student enrollments if total_students is available on the course object. Do not create or modify anything — read-only.

Deliverable: return ONE fenced CSV block with a header row, one row per course in the exact order given in your list, no extra columns:
course_id,course_name,assignment_count,quiz_count,discussion_count,student_count,faculty_count
Use the course names as given above (with term in parentheses). After the CSV block you may add at most 3 lines of caveats (e.g., any endpoint that errored). Nothing else.
Collect Canvas course metrics

Context: I am preparing an accreditation curriculum review for an open university. The audit must show research integration: scholarly literature supporting the pedagogical approaches used in the curriculum. I need one strong, real, verifiable paper for each of five topics.

Use mcp__scholarly__search-arxiv (preferred) and/or mcp__scholarly__search-google-scholar. Search each of the following topics and select ONE clearly relevant paper per topic:

1. "active learning in higher education"
2. "assessment best practices in education"
3. "online learning effectiveness"
4. "curriculum design frameworks"
5. "student engagement strategies"

For each topic, choose a paper that is genuinely relevant (not just keyword overlap), ideally well-cited/foundational (e.g., for active learning, Freeman et al.'s meta-analysis would be ideal if findable; for engagement, Tinto or similar). Record:
- Search_Topic: the exact topic string above
- Paper_Title: exact title
- Authors: author list as returned (comma-separated; may shorten to first 5 + "et al." if very long)
- Relevance_Note: 1-2 sentences explaining how this paper supports that pedagogical approach in a university curriculum

Deliverable: return exactly one fenced CSV block with header:
Search_Topic,Paper_Title,Authors,Relevance_Note
with exactly 5 data rows, one per topic in the order listed. Quote titles/notes properly if they contain commas (use double quotes). After the CSV block, add a short list of the sources found (arXiv IDs or venue/year) for verification. Nothing else.
Scholarly literature search

Task: Create a page in the team's Notion knowledge base titled exactly "Accreditation Review Report". This is for a university accreditation review. You MUST succeed in creating this page; parent-argument validation can be finicky — read the notes below.

KNOWN CONTEXT (verified by me already):
- The Notion workspace currently contains one top-level page: title "Accreditation Documents", page_id "de25d706-d203-42d8-ab4c-4229605f8a39" (you can confirm with mcp__notion__API-post-search).
- Preferred parent for the new page: that page_id. Fallback parent if child creation is impossible: workspace root, i.e. parent = {"workspace": true}.

IMPORTANT — parent validation quirks observed when calling mcp__notion__API-post-page (worth trying, in order):
1) {"type": "page_id", "page_id": "de25d706-d203-42d8-ab4c-4229605f8a39"}
2) {"page_id": "de25d706-d203-42d8-ab4c-4229605f8a39"}
3) {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true}
4) {"workspace": true}
5) parent as a JSON string, e.g. the string value: {"type": "page_id", "page_id": "de25d706-d203-42d8-ab4c-4229605f8a39"}
If ALL shapes are rejected with "Invalid args ... /parent must be object" or similar, do not give up: also try combining the accepted parent shape with a smaller `children` array (e.g., create the page first with NO children and NO icon, then append the body afterwards with mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children using the returned page id). patch-block-children block_id accepts a page id and its block_id parameter is a plain string, so appending works reliably.

PAGE SPEC:
Title (exact, required): Accreditation Review Report
Icon: 🎓 (optional; skip if it causes errors)

Body content to include (use headings_h2, paragraphs, bulleted_list_item, numbered_list_item, callout, and a divider block as appropriate):

Callout (first block): "Curriculum audit of all institution courses against the Higher Education Quality Council accreditation requirements (standards_version 2025.1): minimum 15 courses offered, at least 1 faculty member per course, minimum one assessment (quiz or assignment) per course, maximum student-to-faculty ratio 600:1, and research integration evidenced by at least 5 scholarly references."

H2 "Overall Compliance"
Paragraph: "Overall compliance rate: 81.82% — 18 of 22 courses are compliant. The institution offers 22 courses (meeting the minimum of 15), every course has at least one assessment and at least one faculty member, and 5 peer-reviewed sources support the curriculum's pedagogical approach. 4 courses fail accreditation criteria."

H2 "Non-Compliant Courses"
Paragraph: "All four non-compliant courses fail on the same criterion: their student-to-faculty ratio exceeds the 600:1 maximum. Each has adequate assessment coverage (assignments and/or quizzes present)."
- "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) — ratio 1141.5:1 (2,283 students, 2 faculty)"
- "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014) — ratio 832.67:1 (2,498 students, 3 faculty)"
- "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014) — ratio 806.5:1 (1,613 students, 2 faculty)"
- "Foundations of Finance (Spring 2014) — ratio 750:1 (1,500 students, 2 faculty)"

H2 "Key Metrics"
- "Total courses audited: 22"
- "Compliant courses: 18"
- "Non-compliant courses: 4"
- "Compliance rate: 81.82%"
- "Total faculty across all courses (teachers + TAs): 70"
- "Average student-to-faculty ratio: 488.65:1"
- "Supporting scholarly papers found: 5"

H2 "Scholarly Literature Supporting the Pedagogical Approach"
Paragraph: "Research integration requirement satisfied: 5 peer-reviewed, highly cited works support the curriculum's main pedagogical approaches (minimum required: 5)."
- "Active learning: Freeman et al., 'Active Learning Increases Student Performance in Science, Engineering, and Mathematics' (PNAS, 2014) — meta-analysis of 225 studies; active learning raises exam performance ~0.5 SD and cuts failure rates 55%."
- "Assessment best practices: Angelo & Cross, 'Classroom Assessment Techniques: A Handbook for College Teachers' (1993) — canonical handbook of 50 formative/summative assessment techniques."
- "Online learning effectiveness: Means et al., 'Evaluation of Evidence-Based Practices in Online Learning: A Meta-Analysis and Review of Online Learning Studies' (U.S. Dept. of Education, 2009) — online/blended learning at least as effective as face-to-face instruction."
- "Curriculum design frameworks: Wiggins & McTighe, 'Understanding by Design: A Framework for Curriculum Development' (2005) — backward design aligning objectives, assessments, and instruction."
- "Student engagement strategies: Carini, Kuh & Klein, 'Student Engagement and Student Learning: Testing the Linkages' (Research in Higher Education, 2006) — engagement positively linked to critical thinking, grades, and persistence."

H2 "Recommendations Before the Accreditation Visit"
1) "Recruit/assign additional teachers and teaching assistants to the 4 flagged courses (Foundations of Finance Fall 2013 & Spring 2014, Creative Computing & Culture Fall 2014, Biochemistry & Bioinformatics Spring 2014) so each course's student-to-faculty ratio falls at or below 600:1 — e.g., Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) needs at least 2 more faculty to reach the threshold."
2) "Rebalance enrolment caps or add parallel sections for oversubscribed courses rather than relying solely on hiring."
3) "Add quizzes to the 8 courses currently without any (required assessment types include quiz, assignment, and discussion); all courses currently meet the minimum of one assessment, but a balanced assessment mix strengthens the accreditation evidence."
4) "Maintain and refresh the scholarly literature mapping each term so research integration remains continuously evidenced (requirement: at least 5 scholarly references)."
5) "Re-run this compliance audit after staffing changes and attach the updated Curriculum_Review.xlsx compliance matrix to the accreditation dossier."

Divider, then final paragraph: "Full per-course data is available in the compliance matrix: Curriculum_Review.xlsx (sheets: Course Compliance, Literature Support, Summary). Prepared by the accreditation coordination team ahead of the Higher Education Quality Council visit."

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (verify before reporting done):
- Page exists with title containing the exact phrase "Accreditation Review Report".
- Body contains: the 81.82% compliance rate, the 4 non-compliant course names, the 5 literature references, and the recommendations.
- Verify by calling mcp__notion__API-retrieve-a-page on the new page id AND mcp__notion__API-get-block-children to confirm content.

Deliverable to me: the new page id, its title, its parent page id (or "workspace root"), and a one-line confirmation that verification passed. If, and only if, every creation route fails after genuine attempts (all 5 parent shapes + create-empty-then-append), report the exact error messages you saw.
Create Notion accreditation report page
